findings.summary: Six requests reduce decoder tile use but worsen evaluator p50 latency by 5.8%. Retain eight requests and four drafts; the recent tuning trials have reached a plateau.
observations: NACA ordinary-call median is 2.351 s; rendering + OCR accounts for 93.9% of mean wall time and embedding 5.2%. Instrumented frozen outputs passed.

Across four bounded 32-iteration captures, narrow output/down projections used one row tile in 95 iterations and two in none. The intended tile reduction occurred, but it did not improve full-PDF performance.
Every recognizer peaked at six running requests and two waiting requests with admission still eight. Lower server concurrency brought back a request queue.
GPU busy averages 68–81% across seven one-second samples per device. These values measure kernel activity, not percentage of peak compute or bandwidth.
Both configurations passed all 60 evaluator calls and 5,580 raw EOS completions. Six requests worsened p50 latency by 5.8%, left p95 flat and lowered throughput 0.8%.

The latest identical eight-request control is 1.9% faster at p50 than its predecessor, exceeding the three-draft trial’s 1.0% gain. Recent alternatives have not established an improvement beyond repeat variation.
findings.next_step: Retain eight requests/GPU, four drafts, fixed 32-row tiles, worker rendering and four-GPU compiled embeddings. Close this sweep; any later change needs a new measured hypothesis.
